business_scope.primary_industry_name: Authorized Economic Operator (AEO) Certification and Security Auditing

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Egypt (nationwide unitary jurisdiction; no separate sub-state corporate registry)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid (Civil Law codified system rooted in the Napoleonic tradition with Islamic Sharia as a principal source of legislation per Article 2 of the 2014 Constitution; commercial company law governed by Companies Law No. 159 of 1981 and the Civil Code No. 131 of 1948)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Agreement Establishing the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA, 2019; Investment Protocol adopted 2021)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Companies Law No. 159 of 1981 as amended (including by Law No. 155 of 2019 introducing mandatory beneficial ownership registers); Executive Regulations of the Companies Law (Prime Ministerial Decree No. 96 of 1982 as amended); Egyptian Anti-Money Laundering Law No. 80 of 2002 (as amended by Laws No. 36 of 2014, No. 137 of 2015 and No. 154 of 2019); Executive Regulations of the AML Law (Prime Ministerial Decree No. 2776 of 2003 as amended); Financial Regulatory Authority (FRA) Board of Directors decisions implementing the Beneficial Owners Register; GAFI implementing procedures for incorporation; Central Bank of Egypt AML/CFT rulebooks and Egyptian Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Combating Unit (EMLCU) directives.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Memorandum of Association (Articles of Incorporation) of the Egyptian LLC in Arabic, authenticated by GAFI
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Egyptian Notary Public (Shahrat Al-Tawthiq) / GAFI Authentication Office
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization (only if executed outside Egypt for foreign filing purposes; domestic execution requires Arabic-language notarization and GAFI/Commercial Registry endorsement)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Corporate Power of Attorney granted by the foreign corporate shareholder to the Egyptian incorporation agent or licensed attorney
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign parent company (notarized by a notary in its home jurisdiction)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board resolution (or shareholders' resolution) of the foreign parent approving the formation of the Egyptian LLC and appointing its directors and signatories
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors or shareholders' general meeting of the parent company

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copies of passports / national identity documents of each director, shareholder and ultimate beneficial owner (UBO)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National passport authority or registration authority of the holder's country
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization (combined with Arabic certification by a licensed translator)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Commercial Extract / Certificate of Incumbency of the foreign corporate shareholder (if a corporate entity is a shareholder)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registry or licensed corporate-services provider in the shareholder's jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: UBO Declaration Form for the FRA/GAFI Beneficial Owners Register, executed by each UBO before an Egyptian notary or Egyptian consulate abroad
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Egyptian Notary Public / Egyptian Ministry of Foreign Affairs Authentication Department / Egyptian diplomatic mission

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based customer due diligence under Law No. 80 of 2002 and CBE AML/CFT instructions for all directors, shareholders and UBOs. Screening is required against: the EMLCU national Sanctions (terrorist financing) list, NAMLAC designations, United Nations Security Council consolidated sanctions, OFAC SDN List, EU consolidated sanctions, and UK sanctions. Politically Exposed Persons (foreign and domestic) require senior management approval, documented source of wealth and source of funds, and enhanced ongoing monitoring for a minimum of 12 months following cessation of public office. Enhanced due diligence applies to shell-company ownership chains, complex nominee structures, and any AEO (Authorized Economic Operator) applicant or customs-broker nexus under Customs Law No. 207 of 2020 and WCO SAFE Framework requirements.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) One-Stop-Shop (OSS) 'Invest in Egypt' electronic incorporation platform (https://www.gafi.gov.eg); downstream registration on the Egyptian Commercial Registry network administered by the Ministry of Trade and Industry
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The LLC's statutory corporate name must be in Arabic; the Arabic name governs registration, publication, tax files and legal personality. One Latin-script transliteration may be registered as a complementary trade name, provided the Arabic spelling remains the authoritative version. The name must contain a distinguishing element, reflect or be consistent with the corporate objects, must not be identical or confusingly similar to existing GAFI-reserved or Commercial Registry names, must not be misleading, and the LLC suffix 'شركة ذات مسئولية محدودة' (limited-liability company indicator) must be appended. A purely foreign-language name is acceptable only if transliterated into Arabic script for the statutory petition.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon GAFI name rejection, the applicant's licensed Egyptian attorney may submit a written administrative appeal in Arabic to the GAFI Legal Affairs Appellate Committee within 15 working days of the electronic rejection decision, attaching the system-generated refusal record, the proposed name list and supporting arguments on distinctiveness and compliance with GAFI naming rules. A reserved name may be extended for one additional reservation period (normally another 30 days) by payment of the GAFI extension fee, provided the name has not been granted to a third party in the meantime. If the appellate committee upholds the rejection, the applicant may bring an annulment action before the Administrative Litigation Division of the Egyptian State Council (Majlis al-Dawla) within 30 days of notification of the final administrative decision, acting through a lawyer admitted to the Egyptian Bar.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not accepted as a purely virtual or PO-Box-only address. The LLC must maintain a physical registered office in Egypt proven by a lease, ownership title or free-zone usufruct instrument, and must notify the GAFI One-Stop-Shop, Commercial Registry, Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) and Social Insurance Authority. A serviced-office address or licensed business center satisfying physical occupancy and mail-delivery requirements is tolerated for a consultancy and audit-risk business, but the address is the statutory tax and civil domicile under Income Tax Law No. 91 of 2005 and VAT Law No. 67 of 2016. For the customs-AEO-supply-chain-audit scope, the Customs Authority expects demonstrable commercial substance, personnel availability and client-file access; a serviced office is acceptable only where the landlord provides dedicated physical workspace and registered-mail services.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low-to-moderate statutory inspection risk. Quantified guidance: approximately 15% estimated probability in the first 36 months of an unannounced visit by the Egyptian Tax Authority or GAFI for a standard-risk, office-based consultancy. Customs AEO-program audits occur by scheduled appointment; unannounced customs inspection is unlikely except where customs-broker licensure or controlled-goods activity is later added.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Bank published fee schedule and minimum-deposit/due-diligence charge

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Egyptian Companies Law No. 159 of 1981 (as amended), Limited Liability Company provisions under Articles 505-575, and its Executive Regulations; Investment Law No. 72 of 2017 (as amended) and Executive Regulations on entity establishment; Commercial Registry Law No. 34 of 1975; Customs Law No. 207 of 2020 (conditional AEO matters).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) - Investor Services One-Stop Shop, in coordination with the Commercial Registry offices of the Ministry of Supply and Internal Trade.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Contract of Incorporation and Articles of Association (Aqd al-Ta'sis / al-Nizam al-Asasi), submitted on GAFI's unified incorporation notification form.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for LLCs under Law 159/1981; shareholders freely determine the capital, which must be divided into equal non-negotiable quotas and fully paid in cash or in-kind at formation. No mandatory escrow account is required for LLC incorporation; escrow rules apply only if a separately regulated activity (e.g., banking, insurance) is added later.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: APPROVED BY THE FOUNDING SHAREHOLDERS OF EG-LLC: (1) The share capital, as specified in the Contract of Incorporation, is fully subscribed and divided into equal non-negotiable quotas; (2) the Articles of Association are adopted, and the signatories are authorized to file the Contract with the General Authority for Investment and Free Zones and to complete Commercial Registry registration; (3) the registered office is established at the address listed in the Articles; (4) [Name/Passport No.] is appointed General Manager and [Name] Compliance Officer, each authorized to execute banking, tax, social insurance, customs, and licensing matters; (5) all pre-incorporation expenses are ratified and paid; (6) this resolution takes effect immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI Investor Services One-Stop Shop (online portal or physical window)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit three alternative name proposals in Arabic and English together with the exact activity description aligned to ISIC 7020 (management consultancy, customs security auditing, AEO advisory). GAFI screens the names against the Commercial Registry index and trademark records. Upon approval, GAFI issues a Name Reservation Certificate valid for two months.
required_dossiers: Proposed company name variants
Copies of founders' passports or national IDs
Detailed activity description referencing ISIC 7020 and customs advisory services
Power of attorney if filed by an agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected for similarity, the applicant may file a modification request with additional alternative names or submit a trademark search certificate; a GAFI grievance committee reviews repeated rejections within 5 working days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution and Notarization of Incorporation Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI Legal Affairs Directorate and Egyptian Notary Public (Shahr al-Aqari)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the bilingual Contract of Incorporation and Articles of Association with Arabic text controlling, covering the trade name, object clause, capital and quotas, registered office address, manager appointments, and governance rules. Each founding shareholder must sign before the Notary Public or authenticate signatures electronically; foreign signatures may be notarized at an Egyptian Consulate abroad. Pay notary fees and contract stamp duty.
required_dossiers: Draft Contract of Incorporation and Articles of Association
Name Reservation Certificate
Passport copies of all founders and appointed managers
Registered office lease contract or allocation letter
Beneficial ownership and AML declaration for each shareholder
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Notary remarks are cured by amending the affected clauses and re-authenticating signatures; if the lease deed is defective, substitute a compliant registered office lease and re-notarize the amended address page.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: GAFI Incorporation Filing and Commercial Registry Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI One-Stop Shop - Commercial Registry Window
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the complete incorporation package through GAFI's Investor Services Center or its online submission portal, pay the prescribed GAFI and Commercial Registry fees, and await the legal review. Under Investment Law No. 72 of 2017, the One-Stop Shop must grant or refuse the registration within 10 working days; simple LLC files are typically cleared earlier. On approval, GAFI registers the LLC in the Commercial Registry and issues the Certificate of Incorporation and the Commercial Registry Extract.
required_dossiers: Notarized Contract of Incorporation and Articles of Association
Name Reservation Certificate
Passport copies of founders and managers
GAFI unified incorporation notification form
Registered office lease contract
Partner declaration form and beneficial ownership statement
Tax registration request form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If GAFI issues observations, submit corrected Arabic documents through the One-Stop Shop correction desk within 15 days; if the statutory 10-working-day deadline is exceeded, file an administrative complaint with GAFI's grievance committee or initiate action before the competent administrative court.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration and Social Insurance Enrollment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) and National Organization for Social Insurance (NOSI)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Using the unified registration form and the Commercial Registry Extract, register the LLC with ETA to obtain the Tax Card, income tax file, and electronic tax account; enroll for VAT if taxable supplies exceed the statutory registration threshold; register any employees and managers with NOSI within 30 days of incorporation and maintain payroll records under Law 91 of 2005 and Law 67 of 2016.
required_dossiers: Commercial Registry Extract
Certificate of Incorporation
Contract of Incorporation and Articles of Association
Registered office lease and utility bill
Tax Card application form
Passports and ID copies of managers and employees
NOSI registration forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: For delayed Tax Card issuance, escalate through the ETA Taxpayer Services Center or the online complaint portal; for NOSI corrections, submit amended employment registration forms and a covering statutory declaration to the competent insurance office.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Bank Account Opening and Company Seal
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial banks licensed by the Central Bank of Egypt
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a corporate bank account using the Commercial Registry Extract, Tax Card, and the apostilled/notarized Contract of Incorporation. Complete the bank's KYC and beneficial ownership procedures, obtain a corporate seal, and register specimen signatures for the General Manager and other authorized signatories.
required_dossiers: Commercial Registry Extract
Tax Card
Certified copy of Contract of Incorporation and Articles of Association
Board/shareholder resolution appointing signatories
Passports of signatories and beneficial owners
Proof of business address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests additional proof of good standing, obtain a Certificate of Good Standing from GAFI and re-submit; if the beneficial owner documentation is queried, provide the corrected AML/KYC declaration and source-of-funds evidence.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Egyptian Customs Authority (ECA) - Customs Registration Department and AEO Committee
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: If the entity will act as a customs broker or maintain a physical storage site under its AEO security program, register with ECA under Customs Law 207 of 2020 to obtain the Import/Export Code and, where applicable, apply for Authorized Economic Operator status after completing the ECA self-assessment questionnaire and submitting the security and fiscal solvency dossier. Pure advisory/audit-only activity does not require this step.
required_dossiers: Commercial Registry Extract
Tax Card
ECA registration application
AEO self-assessment and security procedures manual
Financial solvency certificates and audited statements
Site security and access control documentation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the AEO application is rejected, address the identified security or solvency gaps, resubmit the revised dossier to ECA's AEO Committee, or file an administrative appeal within the statutory 60-day window.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No industrial licensing authority applies to the core advisory/audit activity; if the entity later operates a customs warehouse or physical secure facility, the Egyptian Customs Authority (Law 207 of 2020) and the Industrial Development Authority become the competent bodies.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not required for ISIC 7020 management consultancy and AEO advisory services. A Customs Warehouse License or Industrial Operation License would be required only upon establishment of a physical logistics or storage site.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Egyptian Environmental Affairs Agency (EEAA) - Ministry of Environment
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category C (Environmental Registration) for office-based consultancy and audit activity under Law 4 of 1994 and its amendments; no full EIA is required. If a controlled warehouse or storage facility is added, the project moves to Category B and a limited Environmental Assessment/screening report is required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Office-only activity generates no significant industrial discharge. If warehousing is added, the facility must comply with EEAA standards: wastewater BOD not exceeding 300 mg/L and COD not exceeding 600 mg/L prior to municipal discharge; VOC emissions within the air quality limits of the Executive Regulations; hazardous waste handling and disposal strictly per Law 202 of 2020 through an EEAA-licensed waste carrier.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Certificate from the General Administration of Civil Defense (Ministry of Interior) is required for any physical registered office; structural load and occupancy clearance for the leased premises; workplace safety plan and evacuation procedures under Labor Law 12 of 2003; occupational health cards for all employees. These requirements apply immediately once a physical office is opened, while a virtual-only advisory entity may defer them until site establishment.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) — Maslaha al-Dara'ib al-Misriyah; official portal: https://www.eta.gov.eg; unified e-services and registration: Inataxy (https://inataxy.com); e-invoicing and e-receipt clearance portal: https://einvoicing.eta.gov.eg with API gateway at https://apiportal.invoicing.eta.gov.eg; customs interface is administered separately by the Egyptian Customs Authority (ECA).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: An EG LLC is a resident taxable person. Step 1: incorporate in the Egyptian Commercial Registry and obtain the Chamber of Commerce certificate; Step 2: submit the unified tax registration application through the Inataxy portal or at the competent ETA tax office, attaching certified articles of association, commercial registry extract, registered-office lease, notarized power of attorney, and passports of shareholders and managers; Step 3: ETA inspects the premises and issues the Tax Card containing the single Tax Identification Number / VAT ID; Step 4: complete VAT registration within 30 days of commencing taxable activity or exceeding the EGP 500,000 annual registration threshold; voluntary registration is available above EGP 200,000; Step 5: onboard on the ETA e-invoicing system and activate the digital signature credentials. A non-resident AEO audit consultant with no Egyptian branch may obtain a simplified ETA TIN/VAT ID through an approved local fiscal representative; this ID is mandatory to issue compliant e-invoices and to claim Egyptian export zero-rating.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation — the Egyptian LLC is a separate resident legal person taxed at the corporate income tax rate of 22.5% on worldwide net income; no pass-through or transparent treatment is permitted. Non-resident shareholders are separately taxed on Egyptian-source income under Income Tax Law No. 91 of 2005. Operation inside a designated tax-exempt or free-zone area (e.g., SCZONE) may alter the incidence of CIT and VAT under Investment Law No. 72 of 2017 but does not change the entity-level classification.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Egypt does not operate a check-the-box or US-style entity classification election. Available statutory elections for an EG LLC: (1) Investment Law No. 72 of 2017 free-zone election — substitutes the 22.5% CIT with an annual 1%–2% levy and grants VAT/customs relief for qualifying free-zone export activities; (2) VAT recovery election allowing exporters to elect direct input-VAT credit or refund rather than carrying forward; (3) accelerated depreciation election for fixed assets used in production or information-technology activities; (4) election to treat related supplies separately for the EGP 500,000 VAT registration threshold; and (5) statutory loss carry-forward elections within the six-year period. No hybrid-mismatch elections are currently effective; Egypt’s MLI reservations leave hybrid instruments subject to entity-level taxation.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) under Law No. 67 of 2016 and its Executive Regulations, complemented by the E-Invoicing and E-Receipt mandatory regulations; border measures are set out in Customs Law No. 207 of 2020; specific goods are subject to the 'Table Tax' under Law No. 22 of 2020.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EGP 500,000 of annual taxable supplies (mandatory registration); voluntary registration is permitted once annual taxable turnover exceeds EGP 200,000; non-resident consultancy and digital suppliers without an Egyptian fixed establishment may be caught by reverse-charge purchaser accounting where the recipient bears the VAT obligation.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory phased e-invoicing (B2B/B2G) and e-Receipts (B2C): covered taxpayers must transmit invoice and receipt XML data in real time to the ETA portal via secured REST/SOAP APIs, obtain ETA validation with a digitally stamped QR code on every document, and embed an electronic signature. Documents failing real-time clearance are inadmissible for input-VAT deduction and cannot support export zero-rating. The AEO/LLC must also retain a tamper-evident supply-chain audit trail cross-referenced to ETA clearance IDs.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: 0% VAT applies to: (a) direct exports of movable goods physically leaving Egypt under customs control; (b) exported services, including management consulting, AEO certification audits, and supply-chain security reviews supplied to non-resident clients whose economic benefit is realized abroad, provided consideration is received in convertible foreign currency and the service is not attributable to Egyptian real estate or to an Egyptian fixed establishment; (c) international transport and transit trade; and (d) supplies to free-zone operators. The EG LLC must maintain an export register, corresponding e-invoices coded as zero-rated exports, foreign-currency receipt evidence, and the AEO security-audit documentation to substantiate each claim.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Cleared Egyptian Customs Export Declaration (Bayann Misaddar) or the authorized AEO green-lane manifest
Bill of Lading, Air Waybill, or CMR consignment note proving physical export
Commercial invoice bearing the ETA e-invoicing QR code, VAT line, and Tax Card/TIN details
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank statement evidencing receipt of the export consideration in convertible foreign currency
Certificate of Origin and the export contract or purchase order
AEO supply-chain audit report and security survey records (for the ISIC 7020 service scope)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The ETA and Egyptian Customs Authority re-audit zero-rating claims during AEO compliance cycles. Failure to substantiate export documentation or to repatriate foreign-currency proceeds within the statutory deadline triggers: (i) a VAT clawback assessment at the 14% standard rate with delay ('muddad') penalties of up to 1% per month, capable of compounding to 2%, computed from the original supply date; (ii) a fixed evasion fine of not less than EGP 50,000 and criminal liability for forged export or foreign-exchange certificates under VAT Law Articles 68–71; (iii) forfeiture of input-VAT credit across the entire e-invoice chain; and (iv) administrative sanctions including AEO certificate suspension or revocation, bank-account foreign-exchange restrictions, blacklisting from the export-subsidy program, and loss of customs green-lane clearance privileges.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Egypt (Al-Bank al-Markazi al-Misri); the sole monetary and FX-regulatory authority under Law No. 194 of 2020, with exchange-control, licensing, and supervisory powers over all inward/outward remittances and the interbank FX market.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: As of the March 2024 unified floating regime, the EGP is freely convertible for documented current-account transactions (client audit fees, consulting service settlements, software licensing) through the interbank market, with no mandatory conversion or surrender ratio. Capital-account transactions—share capital subscription, shareholder loans, and dividend/exit repatriation—are fully permitted for companies legalized under Investment Law No. 72 of 2017, but require the receiving bank to register the inflow in the CBE balance-of-payments system and to vet corporate approvals, source of funds, and ETA tax clearances before repatriation. Practical friction is limited to documentary hurdles (audited financials, domiciliation certificates, board resolutions, tax clearance) rather than quantitative or quota-based controls.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: The 2024 CBE modernization abolished the prior export-proceeds surrender obligation; no mandatory percentage of export receipts must now be exchanged into EGP. Repatriation remains compulsory: goods-export proceeds must be received in an Egyptian-licensed bank account within 180 days from the bill of lading date, while service-export proceeds (the relevant category for the EG LLC audit practice) must be received within 90 days from invoice date; one CBE extension of up to 180 days is available for documented justification. Retained FX balances are freely usable for permitted current payments and hedging instruments, subject to CBE monitoring and end-of-month bank reporting.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account / Operational Account (dual mandate)
Capital Escrow Account / Operational Account (dual mandate)
Capital Escrow Account / Operational Account (dual mandate)
Capital Escrow Account / Operational Account (dual mandate)
Capital Escrow Account / Operational Account (dual mandate)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility: Medium for ancillary non-EGP client-fee collection; Low as principal operating rail. Legal constraints: under the Payment and Settlement Systems Law No. 18 of 2019 and CBE licensing rules, unlicensed EMIs (including Wise) cannot legally provide EGP account details, local clearing, or domestic debit/credit rails in Egypt. Wise transfers must terminate as SWIFT or gateway credits into the licensed Egyptian corporate account, and any EGP currency conversion must occur exclusively inside the CBE-banking framework.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is required in principle. CBE AML/CFT rules and Tier-1 bank practice mandate a face-to-face compliance interview for the UBO and at least one authorized signatory of a non-resident-owned LLC; fully remote opening is not permitted. If physical attendance is impossible, the bank accepts a local resident co-signatory acting under a notarized and legally apostilled power of attorney, and the remote UBO must complete biometric-grade video verification before any transaction activity. Allow 2-3 weeks for this enhanced onboarding at NBE, Banque Misr, CIB, or QNB ALAHLI.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident UBO without attested commercial registration and Egyptian tax presence
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified Arabic/English bundle: GAFI establishment certificate, Commercial Registry (CAC) extract, ETA tax card, Ministry of Foreign Affairs legalized constituent documents (MoA/AoA), UBO passport with entry stamp, proof of registered business premise in Cairo or Suez Canal Economic Zone, and corporate chain diagram.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Banking purpose mismatch - high inbound equity funding against nominal consulting-service revenue model
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Treasury mandate declaring receivable collection of AEO certification and supply-chain audit fees; signed engagement letters with client list, fee schedule, expected monthly transaction volume/value thresholds, and a 12-month cash-flow forecast.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusual third-party or intergroup funding not directly aligned with audit client base
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Intercompany agreement, group consolidation chart, board resolution authorizing transfers, audited financial statements of the remitting entity, and legal opinion on the sender's existence and capacity in its home jurisdiction.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk jurisdiction flags, PEP status, or opacity in ultimate beneficial ownership
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: CBE-compliant source-of-wealth declaration supported by 6-month bank statements of the capital provider; sanctions-screening acknowledgement; AML/CTF policy of the audit practice; PEP disclosure with professional license and accessed corporate registers.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant protocol: pre-open a temporary capital subscription account at the selected Tier-1 bank after GAFI pre-registration. The foreign shareholder executes a SWIFT MT103 with Field 70 stating 'EG LLC - Share Capital Contribution under Investment Law No. 72 of 2017'; the receiving bank applies CBE BPM6 purpose code 310 (Direct Investment - Equity Capital), issues a capital domiciliation certificate, and verifies the board resolution, source-of-funds statements, and UBO KYC pack before transferring funds to the operational account. USD/EUR proceeds may be retained without forced conversion; EGP conversion is made only on the client's instruction at the interbank rate. Funds are recorded as paid-in capital, not taxable income, in the subsequent ETA filing.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Service-related disbursements (AEO audit software licenses, subcontract auditor fees) settle via SWIFT MT103 with CBE purpose code 271 (business and management consulting services), backed by the signed service agreement, itemized commercial invoice, ETA-compliant VAT invoice, and the bank's foreign-services payment declaration. Goods-related disbursements (security hardware or audit equipment) require CargoX/ACI pre-registration before shipment and settlement via Commercial Letter of Credit (MT700/MT707) or CBE-accepted documentary collection against transport, insurance, and inspection documents. EGP-denominated high-value payments above EGP 1 million must clear through Egypt's RTGS (E-GP) same-day system; minor payments may use the instant-payment network subject to bank cut-off times.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forward (EGP vs USD or EUR) for contractually determined audit-fee exposure; tenor up to 12 months; must be backed by the underlying client purchase order and CBE trade evidence.

Offshore non-deliverable forward (NDF) on EGP for non-resident counterparties hedging equity exposure; settlement in USD against the CBE reference rate; permitted only when booked through a CBE-licensed bank and prohibited for speculative purposes.
Cross-currency swap (USD/EGP) to match shareholder-loan amortization schedules with operating cash inflows; requires prior CBE approval and an intercompany balance-sheet hedging rationale.

Transactional FX swap for bridging liquidity between the USD/EUR operational account and the EGP tax/operating account; limited to 3% of audited annual turnover and fully evidenced by transaction logs.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax return and annual financial statements submission
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA), Ministry of Finance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within four months after the end of the fiscal year; for a 31 December year-end, the deadline is 30 April.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of EGP 1,000–5,000 per tax period, late-payment interest on assessed tax, enforced collection and seizure proceedings, and possible cancellation of the unified tax card for repeated non-compliance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial Registry Directorate, Ministry of Trade and Industry / GAFI e-Services Portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually during the first quarter of each calendar year; renewal must be completed by 31 March to avoid lapse.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines, prohibition on banking and government transactions, suspension of commercial registration, and administrative strike-off from the Commercial Registry after formal notice.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually in coordination with the commercial registration renewal; the tax card must remain valid for customs, banking and government transactions.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: An invalid tax card prevents customs clearance, import/export operations and government contracting; continued lapse may trigger monetary penalties and administrative suspension of the company's tax file.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual confirmation due by 31 March following the fiscal year-end; any shareholding transfer or change in beneficial ownership must be notified within 30 days.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or update the UBO register may result in administrative fines, suspension of commercial registration renewal, and personal liability under the anti-money-laundering legal framework.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Meeting resolution and statutory register audit
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders' meeting; records remain inspectable by GAFI and the appointed auditor
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Shareholders' approval meeting must be convened within six months of the fiscal year-end; signed minutes must be retained at the registered office.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-convening of the approval meeting may invalidate dividend distributions and corporate filings; managers and directors may be held personally liable for resulting damages.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit is required for an LLC when paid-up capital exceeds EGP 250,000, annual gross revenue exceeds EGP 10,000,000, or when required by the Egyptian Tax Authority or GAFI; a certified audit is also the market-standard requirement for an AEO supply-chain audit advisory LLC.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Egyptian Accounting Standards (EAS) as issued by the Egyptian Society of Accountants and Auditors and enforced by the Egyptian Tax Authority; EAS are substantively aligned with IFRS.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under Egyptian companies law and GAFI beneficial-ownership rules, every Egyptian legal person must maintain an internal beneficial-ownership register; any direct or indirect shareholding transfer or change in ultimate beneficial ownership must be filed with GAFI within 30 days, and an annual confirmation statement must be submitted by 31 March following each fiscal year-end.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book of Shareholders' and Managers' Resolutions

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 250 – 850 per year for a licensed Cairo registered office and corporate secretarial agent
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 1,200 – 4,500 per year for an independent audit of a low-risk AEO consulting LLC

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Egypt offers a statutory corporate income tax rate of 22.5%. Preferential regimes include a reduced rate of 14% for certain manufacturing and export-oriented activities in the Suez Canal Economic Zone (SCZONE), a 10% rate for free-zone companies under the Free Zones Law, and a 5% tax on profits from certain new capital-intensive projects under the Investment Law No. 72 of 2017 subject to geographic and sectoral criteria. The Unified Tax Law No. 91 of 2005 (as amended by Law No. 26 of 2020) provides deductions for social insurance contributions, certain financing costs, and depreciation allowances. A 50% additional deduction is available for qualifying R&D and innovation expenditures, subject to ministerial approval.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form No. 113 (Corporate Income Tax Return) for companies governed by the Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA); electronic filing mandated through the ETA e-filing portal at www.eta.gov.eg or the unified electronic tax system introduced under the Tax Procedures Law No. 53 of 2023.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (fiscal year aligned with the company’s statutory accounting period, defaulting to the calendar year; quarterly advance tax payments are due for companies with prior-year taxable profits exceeding EGP 100,000)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual CIT return must be filed within five months from the end of the fiscal year (e.g., by May 31 for a December 31 year-end). With the ETA’s digital transformation, e-filing deadlines may be extended by Ministerial Decree; but the statutory five-month rule remains the anchor. Quarterly advance payments are due within 30 days of the end of each quarter. The final tax payment is due on the filing deadline.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax card number, commercial registry number, fiscal year start/end dates, and legal form of the entity.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident entities with Egyptian-source income must obtain a temporary tax card and file using the ETA-assigned registration number; a local tax representative is required under Article 7 of the Unified Tax Law.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total worldwide gross revenue for Egyptian tax-resident companies; for non-residents, only Egyptian-source gross revenue.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents must report only Egyptian-source revenues from services rendered in Egypt, IP royalties from Egyptian licensees, interest from Egyptian borrowers, and capital gains from shares in Egyptian companies. No worldwide aggregation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 7 (Cost of Goods Sold and Deductible Expenses)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Itemized operating deductions, including depreciation, direct materials, subcontractor costs, employee wages, and administrative overhead.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents may deduct only expenses directly attributable to producing Egyptian-source revenue. Head-office overhead allocations are deductible only if a valid cost-sharing or head-office expense agreement exists and is supported by the ETA.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net profit after all statutory deductions and adjustments; this is the base before loss carryforward and tax exemptions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents should ensure that intercompany charges (management fees, royalties) are at arm’s length and that any disallowed expenses (entertainment above 1% of turnover, unregistered contracts) are reversed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Amount of previously assessed tax losses utilized in the current year, capped at five consecutive years from the loss year end.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident branch may carry forward its Egyptian branch losses per the same five-year rule; losses from a foreign head office cannot be offset against Egyptian taxable income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reductions applied for investment incentives, such as investment tax credits under Law 72/2017, free-zone exemptions, or SCZONE reduced rates.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident investors must attach the relevant investment license and Customs/Free-Zone Directorate approvals to support any reduced-rate claim.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross corporate income tax computed at 22.5% (or applicable preferential rate) on taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents are subject to the same 22.5% rate on Egyptian-source income, unless a treaty rate applies for dividends, interest, or royalties in a separate withholding regime.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 29 (Foreign Tax Credits and Withholding Credits)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Credits for Egyptian withholding taxes on local income and for foreign taxes paid on Egyptian-source income under DTA provisions, capped at the Egyptian tax attributable to that income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents claiming treaty relief must attach a valid Egyptian Tax Authority Form 5 (TRC) from their home jurisdiction, accompanied by a notarized English translation and legalization by the Egyptian embassy.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty is 2.5% of the tax due (or minimum EGP 500) for the first 30 days, plus 0.5% per week thereafter, capped at 12% of tax due. Late payment penalty is 2% per month or part thereof on unpaid tax, capped at 12% of the tax amount. Non-filing of e-return triggers a separate EGP 10,000 penalty. Failure to submit quarterly advance payment declarations incurs a penalty of 1.5% of the unpaid amount per month, capped at 12%. Persistent failure allows the ETA to automatically assess the tax based on deemed income and to enforce collection via administrative attachment.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% under Article 56 of the Unified Tax Law No. 91/2005 (as amended by Law 26/2020), applicable to all dividends (cash or in-kind) distributed to shareholders, whether resident or non-resident, subject to the satisfaction of the participation exemption for resident corporate shareholders.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: A non-resident shareholder must (a) obtain a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from its home tax authority, (b) submit the TRC to the Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) in original form, legalized or apostilled per Egypt’s treaty commitments, (c) file a treaty relief claim (Form 5) with the ETA’s International Taxation Unit, and (d) await an ETA directive that instructs the Egyptian paying entity to apply the reduced DTA withholding rate at source. Where the DTA rate is lower (e.g., 5% for 25%+ holdings under the OECD-based treaty, or exemption under the Egyptian-UAE treaty), the reduced rate is applied only after ETA pre-approval, otherwise the payer must withhold at the statutory 10% and the non-resident may claim a subsequent refund within five years from the end of the filing year. Required documentation includes the TRC, audited financial statements of the distributing company, a full chain of ownership proof, and a signed declaration of economic substance in the treaty jurisdiction.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: statutory 20% withholding tax on the gross amount paid to non-resident licensors for IP licensed for use in Egypt; treaty relief may reduce to 10-15% under DTA provisions (e.g., Egyptian-Dutch treaty 14%, Egyptian-UAE treaty 5% for patent royalties). Interest: statutory 20% withholding on payments to non-resident lenders on loans used in Egypt, reduced to 10-15% under most treaties, and 0% on certain sovereign-guaranteed or qualifying SCZONE loans under ministerial exemptions. Loan-to-equity ratio exceeding 4:1 results in interest disallowance per Article 30 of the Tax Law. No withholding tax applies to dividends remitted by Egyptian free-zone companies if profits were fully exempt at source, provided the distribution is out of exempt profits.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Mandatory Local File / Master File preparation is required when the taxpayer’s annual gross revenue exceeds EGP 25,000,000, or when intercompany controlled transaction values exceed the thresholds specified in Ministerial Decree No. 285 of 2020: EGP 5,000,000 for tangible goods, EGP 2,000,000 for services, royalties, or financing. Filing of the Master File and Local File with the ETA must occur on or before the annual CIT return deadline, and the Egyptian Statement of Controlled Transactions (Form 26-1) is mandatory regardless of revenue when related-party transactions exist.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Egypt applies the OECD Transfer Pricing Guidelines through Articles 59-61 of the Unified Tax Law and Ministerial Decree No. 285 of 2020. Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) are explicitly required under the Egyptian TP regime: the ETA can disregard transactions lacking genuine economic substance, re-characterize them based on the actual business purpose, and deny deductions for arrangements whose principal purpose is tax avoidance. The CFC rules under Article 61 allow direct attribution of profits from low-taxed controlled foreign entities. While Egypt does not have a codified General Anti-Avoidance Rule (GAAR) as a separate statute, the ETA exercises parity powers and substance-over-form doctrines under Article 29 of the Tax Procedures Law. For SCZONE and free-zone entities, the Free Zones General Authority requires real physical presence, local payroll, and substantive operational activities to preserve tax-exempt status; shell or letterbox companies are automatically disqualified.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion (Tax Procedures Law No. 53/2023, Article 38 and Unified Tax Law)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate falsification of books, issuance of fictitious invoices, underreporting of Egyptian-source revenue, use of shell company structures with no economic effect to shift profits, submission of forged tax certificates, or intentional concealment of taxable transactions to the ETA.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Imprisonment for a term of no less than 3 years and no more than 5 years, plus a monetary fine of EGP 50,000 to EGP 150,000 per tax year involved, or twice the tax evaded. In addition, the ETA imposes a 100% late-payment penalty on the evaded tax amount and disallows all abused deductions. A compliant company found allied in a tax evasion scheme (e.g., accepting fake supplier invoices in the AEO audit scope) is subject to an automatic 5-year accelerated audit, automatic TP re-assessment, and a separate 10% of the underlying tax as a gross negligence penalty.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Islamic and civil jurisprudence in Egypt allows the ETA to pierce the corporate veil when the company is a mere alter ego of its directors, is undercapitalized at formation, or has been used to evade taxes in bad faith. Directors face personal civil restitution for the full amount of evaded tax plus 100% surcharge, are subject to travel bans under the ETA’s Executive Regulations, and may be personally named in criminal prosecution. Fraudulent dissolution or asset stripping to avoid tax liabilities renders directors jointly and severally liable without fiscal year limitation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Mispricing / Absence of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to prepare or file Local File / Master File when exceeding the EGP 25,000,000 revenue threshold; use of non-arm’s length prices (e.g., services provided to a related overseas company at a marked-down fee); a controlled transaction concluded without documentation of comparable analysis or without supporting agreements; the ETA re-characterization of a service contract as a distribution of hidden profits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Adjustment of taxable income to arm’s length, imposition of an additional penalty of 20% on the tax under-assessed, and a late-payment penalty of 1.5% per month on the additional tax. In egregious cases, the ETA disallows the entire related-party deduction. For a customs-AEO entity, the TP adjustment triggers a customs valuation re-audit and potential revocation of AEO certification.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly signed false TP documentation or instructed the fabrication of a transfer pricing study are exposed to imprisonment under Article 38 of the Law on Fraudulent Tax Offenses, personal civil liability for the full tax adjustment, asset freezes, and cancellation of the company’s AEO authorization. Travel bans are routinely imposed during the ETA’s tax fraud investigation phase.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company Abuse / Illegal Regulatory Arbitrage (Company Law and ESR Framework)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Registration of an Egyptian LLC with no local office, staff, or operational capacity, created solely to obtain free-zone tax exemption while channeling foreign services through a purported Egyptian taxable nexus; providing false substance declarations to the tax authority.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Immediate revocation of tax exemption, retroactive taxation for the prior five fiscal years at the full 22.5% rate plus 14% annual interest, a fine of up to EGP 500,000 and an additional 50% of the evaded tax as a civil penalty. The company’s commercial registration may be struck off and its free-zone license withdrawn.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Under Egypt’s economic substance enforcement policy, directors of shell LLCs face personal liability for all tax debts, are disqualified from forming any new Egyptian company for 5 years, and may be subject to criminal sanctions if the shell is used for money laundering. Multiple shell structures used to evade TP rules trigger money laundering charges under Law No. 80 of 2002, carrying imprisonment of up to 15 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML / CFT Deficiency in AEO Supply Chain Audit
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to file or deliberately omitting operating income on tax returns while maintaining unexplained cash flow or wire transfers routed through third-party jurisdictions inconsistent with the business model (e.g., WISE or Wire Transfer payments received from unknown shell counterparties); failure to maintain the required KYC files and audit trails in the customs AEO certification scope; allowing the entity to be used as a pass-through for tax-evasion proceeds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Law No. 80 of 2002 (Anti-Money Laundering Law), the ETA and the Egyptian Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Combating Unit (EMLCU) can impose fines up to EGP 5,000,000 on the entity, freeze all accounts, and confiscate assets equivalent to the proceeds. AEO certification is automatically withdrawn, and the entity is barred from any customs facility for 8 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally liable civilly for the full amount laundered, are imprISOned for up to 15 years, and face permanent disqualification from bank signatory roles. Under the Customs Authority’s mandatory reporting requirements, any director knowingly complicit in AML breaches is subject to a ban on travel, direct seizure of personal passport, and a lifetime bar on holding AEO-related company directorships.
